title: Equivalences between pattern-fibered objects detected over base edges
statement:
Use categorical patterns, marked objects over $\bar C$, and $\mathfrak P$-fibered objects from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], marked products from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], categorical equivalences of simplicial sets from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and weak homotopy equivalences from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\})$ be any small fully scaled pattern, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of $\mathfrak P$-fibered marked objects over $\bar C$. Put $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A,Z)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Z)$. The following are equivalent:

(1) For every $\mathfrak P$-fibered $Z$, restriction $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(X,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

(2) For every edge $e:\Delta^1\to C$, including degenerate edges and edges outside $S$, the induced underlying simplicial map $X\times_C\Delta^1\to Y\times_C\Delta^1$ is a categorical equivalence.

The objects in (2) are quasicategories. There is no assumption that every edge of $C$ lies in $S$, and (2) does not assert that vertex fibers alone suffice.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4, equivalence (1) with (3), printed pp.1483-1485. Its vertex-only variant is not used. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.
